Participants were excluded if they spent less than 20 minutes interacting with the systems or completed fewer than two NarrativeLoom story beats. Counts excluded separately for each reason are not reported. Neither 109 nor 94 is identified as a randomized count; retain n_randomized = null.
corrections.quote: To maintain high data quality, participants were excluded if they spent less than 20 minutes interacting with the systems or completed fewer than two story beats in the NarrativeLoom condition.

corrections.form_value: All three recorded outcomes leave measure_detail, ai_available_when_produced, and timing as empty strings.
corrections.source_says: For all three recorded TTCW outcomes, set ai_available_when_produced = yes and timing = immediate: the scored stories were produced during the AI system-interaction sessions, with no delayed writing assessment reported. Describe the TTCW scoring in measure_detail: each expert independently assigns binary pass/fail judgments; the overall score counts tests passed out of 14, while originality and elaboration each comprise three criteria. Originality concerns unique ideas, absence of cliches, and structural/format innovation; elaboration concerns sensory believability, character complexity, and layers of meaning. The aggregation underlying t(79) remains unspecified, so the existing caution and null analysis unit should remain.
corrections.quote: Each expert independently provided a binary pass or fail assessment for each test, accompanied by a brief justification. A story’s final creativity score is the total number of tests passed (0–14).

confirmed: Source version and scope are correct: arXiv:2603.07155v1, 7 March 2026, CHI-formatted manuscript, 19 PDF pages; the complete markdown was read through its final references, with no appendix or supplement identified in this document (PDF p. 1 version stamp; p. 2 ACM Reference Format; pp. 17-19 end matter).

The formative study recruited five writers with prior AI-writing-tool experience for approximately one-hour interviews; it did not randomly assign AI assistance or score creative-task outputs (PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1.1-3.1.2; p. 4, Table 1).

The main study analyzed 50 people, meeting the study-level threshold exactly; both condition counts refer to the same within-person sample. The expert-rated subset must not be treated as 50 independently scored writers (PDF p. 9, Sections 5.1-5.2; pp. 10 and 13, Sections 5.4 and 6.5).

No randomized people study is confirmed: system order is described only as counterbalanced. Random sampling of stories and randomized story presentation to raters do not establish random assignment of participants to condition order. Retain randomized = not_stated, S2 design_class = other, core = unclear, and context_class = none; has_randomized_people_study = false means not documented, not proven non-random (PDF p. 9, Section 5.2; p. 10, Section 5.4; p. 13, Section 6.5).

Both systems used GPT-4o for story generation, with the same initial sparkle; participants used each for 20 minutes after a 3-minute tutorial, and NarrativeLoom required at least two story beats (PDF p. 9, Section 5.2).

Four experts evaluated the story subset. Section 6.5 reports 20 story pairs comprising 40 stories, whereas Section 5.4 says each expert pair evaluated the same set of 10 story pairs before reporting 20 pairs and 40 stories across expert pairs. The form correctly flags this ambiguity; the distinct writer count and aggregation underlying t(79) are not stated (PDF p. 10, Section 5.4 and Table 3; p. 13, Section 6.5; p. 14, Quantitative Preference and Creativity Scores).

S2-O1 and the one-line finding reproduce the printed overall TTCW result: NarrativeLoom M = 9.72 out of 14, SD = 2.1; chatbot M = 5.00 out of 14, SD = 1.8; paired t(79) = 13.68, p < 0.001 (PDF p. 14, Section 6.5).

S2-O2 reproduces the printed originality result: NarrativeLoom M = 1.07 out of 3 versus chatbot M = 0.38; t(79) = 6.16, p = 0.001. The form also correctly notes that Figure 9 instead marks the comparison with three asterisks defined as p < 0.001 (PDF p. 14, Section 6.5; p. 15, Figure 9).
S2-O3 reproduces the printed elaboration result: NarrativeLoom M = 1.95 out of 3 versus chatbot M = 1.07; t(79) = 8.31, p < 0.001 (PDF p. 14, Section 6.5).

The expert TTCW judgments are scored on produced stories, so criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output = met is supported. User-perceived diversity concerns available narrative possibilities, not similarity across different people's outputs (PDF pp. 9-10, Sections 5.3.1 and 5.4, Table 4; p. 11, Section 6.1).

This is an original system evaluation with a formative interview study and a main user study, not a synthesis; leaving the synthesis defaults is appropriate (PDF p. 3, Section 3; pp. 9-10, Section 5).
summary: The arXiv v1 supports 50 analyzed participants and all three reported TTCW results, but does not establish randomized condition order. Corrections add exclusion details, seven omitted output outcomes, and missing outcome and contrast metadata.
